prerequisites: C.G.1. Capacity for analysis and synthesis
C.G.2. Capacity for organization and planning
C.G.20. Ability to apply theoretical knowledge in practice

C.E.1. Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
C.E.2. Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application to solving engineering problems.

learning_outcomes.text: Analyze the geometry, position, and displacement of mechanisms.
Perform kinematic and dynamic analysis of mechanisms.
Analyze the movement of machines independently of the forces acting on them, i.e., study kinematic problems of position, velocity, acceleration.
Dynamically analyze the machine considering the forces that originate its movement and the inertia forces resulting from it.
Design mechanisms to meet specific mobility requirements.
Raise awareness in the design of sustainable and environmentally friendly machines and mechanisms, fulfilling SDG 9 (sustainable industrialization) and SDG 12 (promoting sustainable production).
Acquire proficiency in solving typical problems of mechanism kinematics such as the calculation of positions, velocities, and accelerations, as well as in the handling of dynamic analysis techniques.
Understand the initial concepts of mechanical design to guide in the generation of mechanisms that perform specific mechanical functions.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.

syllabus_topics: BLOQUE TEMÁTICO I: Introduction: Machine and mechanism
Tema 1. Machine and mechanism. Geometry of motion
BLOQUE TEMÁTICO II: Kinematics of machines
Tema 2. Kinematics of mechanisms and machines
Application to mechanisms and machine elements.
BLOQUE TEMÁTICO III: Dynamics of machines
Tema 3. Dynamics of mechanisms and machines
Application to mechanisms and machine elements.
BLOQUE TEMÁTICO IV: Synthesis of mechanisms
Introduction to the geometric synthesis of mechanisms.
teaching_methods: Self-study problem and/or practical case solving
Evaluation tests for theoretical and practical content
Written tests consisting of problem-solving, questions, and/or practical cases (MD-7)
Theoretical classes accompanied by the resolution of a collection of problems (MD-1, MD-3)
Autonomous practical cases and/or questionnaires by the student (MD-2, MD-3, MD-7)
assessment_rules: The general evaluation model is continuous evaluation. No individual evaluation activity can exceed 60% of the global grade. Non-re-evaluable activities cannot exceed 40% of the global grade and generally should not have a minimum score, unless they are practical activities. SE-1 and SE-3 require a minimum score of 4, while SE-2 has no explicit minimum. To pass the course, the final weighted average must be 5 points (out of 10) or higher, provided all activities with minimum scores are met. 100% attendance to laboratory and computer lab practices is mandatory; unexcused absence from any practice results in a failing grade of 0 for the entire subject. In the extraordinary call, students will only re-take non-passed re-evaluable activities (score below the minimum), retaining scores from non-re-evaluable activities. If all re-evaluable activities are passed but the overall grade is still below 5, students will re-take re-evaluable activities where they scored below 5, or if all re-evaluable activities scored 5 or above, they must take the final written test (SE-1).
